newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest hogs off $1.50-$2, few trades - private.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest hogs off $1.50-$2, few trades - private.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices were mostly bid $1.50 to $2.00 per cwt lower, with few trades reported also at prices $1.50 to $2.00 lower, livestock dealers and packer buyers said.
"Everybody's got today's slaughter put together and aren't even looking for more," one Illinois hog buyer said.
Weak margins and lower pork prices cooled packer interest for weekend slaughter, they said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs were $1.50 per cwt lower, with a few trading at $55.50 to $56.00 in the country and $56.00 to $57.00 at plants that were buying hogs.
Illinois hog sales were not well established, with bids $1.50 lower at $55.50 to $56.00 in the country and $57.00 at plants. Few trades were reported at that level, dealers said.
Indiana hogs were bid $2.00 lower at $54.00 in the country and $57.50 at plants.
"When you talk $1.00 to $2.00 lower, they (farmers) hang up the phone real fast," one Indiana dealer said. "We're trying to get them to stop shipping hogs, and it appears to be working" he said.
